issues.description: SubPageTable initialization creates a root frame but leaves its executable permission resource absent and relies on an invariant that inconsistently treats the same key as both a frame index and a physical address.
issues.rationale: The initialized state-machine frames map contains the root at p.addr(), but the executable SubPageTable uses HashMap::new() for perms. Its written invariant requires every frame key to have a permission entry, while also interpreting the quantified key as an index in PHYSICAL_BASE + i * SIZEOF_FRAME and frame_index_to_addr(i), so the empty and mis-keyed representation cannot establish wf without the explicit assume. Repair bc92f16a consistently uses physical-address keys, inserts p.addr() -> (p, Tracked(pt)), and changes assume(wf) to assert(wf). The allocator postcondition supplies the normalized address-validity fact needed by this same repair; it is not an independent defect.

issues.verification: Immutable source and direct repair-diff adjudication by two reviewers. The empty permission map contradicts written frame/permission membership, and the repair removes the exact initialization trust boundary. Historical Rust/Verus was not executed.
